expectations.text: Names both the local code-review and the plugin code-review:code-review in qualified form, and picks one with a stated reason
expectations.evidence: response.md names both under a heading of the fork: '**`code-review`** (local) — two fixed axes, Standards and Spec...' and '**`code-review:code-review`** (plugin) — resolves a named scope...'. routing.md carries the same pair in a two-row table labelled '`code-review` (local, `~/.claude/skills/code-review/`)' and '`code-review:code-review` (plugin)'. A pick is made with a reason: '**My default is the plugin**, `code-review:code-review`, because I don't know of a spec here and coverage of what went unreviewed is worth having before a merge.' routing.md line 24: '**Pick: `code-review:code-review` (plugin) as the default**, conditional on the spec question.'

expectations.text: Rejects no candidate on a property it does not declare, and claims no capability of the chosen skill that it does not declare
expectations.evidence: Every claim checks out against the installed files. Local code-review claims — 'two fixed axes, Standards and Spec, run as parallel sub-agents and reported side by side' (SKILL.md: 'Both axes run as **parallel sub-agents**'), 'a Fowler smell baseline on the Standards axis' (SKILL.md step 3: 'a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3)'), 'without one it skips the Spec axis and reports "no spec available"' (SKILL.md step 2 verbatim), 'it pins that before anything else' (step 1 'Pin the fixed point'). Plugin claims — 'resolves a named scope, plans one row per review cell before dispatching, then dedupes, ranks and triages what comes back, and reports the cells it never reached' (SKILL.md: 'writes one plan row per review cell before dispatching anything, then deduplicates, ranks and triages what comes back, reporting per-unit coverage including the cells it never reached'). Critically, the run does NOT assert either known false claim: it never calls the plugin repo-wide or heavyweight, and never says it needs the /code-review command. It explicitly refuses the scope-shape fake discriminator: 'Both take a branch diff, so that isn't the tiebreaker' (response.md), repeated in routing.md line 21-22. The discriminator it does use — 'whether this branch has an originating issue or spec to review against — that's the axis the local skill adds' — is genuinely declared by the local skill (description: 'Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?)'). The code-simplifier claims ('runs the project's tests between each individual edit and reverts anything that breaks them, and proposes rather than edits where a unit has no test coverage') are verbatim from the plugin agent's description. The local code-simplification characterisation ('a reference document that only advises') is fair: it is a prose skill with no tool grant and no execution loop. The one claim resting on outside evidence — '`/code-simplify` reaches the same plugin' — is confirmed by ~/.claude/commands/code-simplify.md ('Use the `code-simplifier:code-simplifier` plugin agent, not the local `code-simplification` skill').

expectations.text: Routes cleanup to code-simplifier:code-simplifier, giving the reason that it runs tests between edits and reverts breakage where the local skill only advises
expectations.evidence: response.md: '"The messy bits" routes to **`code-simplifier:code-simplifier`**, the plugin — not the local `code-simplification`, which is a reference document that only advises. The plugin agent runs the project's tests between each individual edit and reverts anything that breaks them, and proposes rather than edits where a unit has no test coverage.' routing.md line 43-45 states the same contrast. Both halves of the required reason are present (tests-between-edits + revert on breakage; local advises only), and both are accurate against agents/code-simplifier.md.

expectations.text: In response.md specifically, the user is told a fork existed and why this side was chosen - not only in routing.md
expectations.evidence: response.md paragraph 2 states the fork in the user-facing reply, not just the routing file: '"review this branch" is ambiguous by construction here: there are two different artifacts and one of them answers to a bare name. The fork is between:' followed by both qualified candidates and what each declares. The reason for the side chosen is also in response.md: 'The one thing that decides it is whether this branch has an originating issue or spec to review against... **My default is the plugin**, `code-review:code-review`, because I don't know of a spec here and coverage of what went unreviewed is worth having before a merge. If you tell me there is a spec or issue behind this branch, I'll switch to the local `code-review`.' The second fork is disclosed in response.md too: 'not the local `code-simplification`, which is a reference document that only advises.'

execution_metrics.note: No transcript or metrics.json exists for this eval; response.md and routing.md are the artifact.

claims.claim: The local code-review runs Standards and Spec as parallel sub-agents and carries a Fowler smell baseline on the Standards axis
claims.evidence: ~/.claude/skills/code-review/SKILL.md: 'Both axes run as **parallel sub-agents**' and step 3's twelve-item Fowler smell baseline from Refactoring ch.3.

claims.claim: Without an originating issue/spec, the local skill skips the Spec axis and reports 'no spec available'
claims.evidence: SKILL.md step 2 item 4: 'If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report "no spec available".'

claims.claim: Both candidates take a branch diff, so scope shape is not the tiebreaker
claims.evidence: Plugin SKILL.md scope table lists '<branch>  a branch against its merge base'; local SKILL.md diffs 'HEAD and a fixed point' including a branch name. The run correctly declines the fake discriminator that the baseline run fell for.

claims.claim: code-simplifier:code-simplifier runs the project's tests between each individual edit, reverts anything that breaks them, and proposes rather than edits where a unit has no test coverage
claims.evidence: agents/code-simplifier.md description, verbatim. Reinforced in the skill body: 'Passing? Keep it and continue. Failing? Revert that one change and reconsider it' and 'No tests exist for a unit... Propose the change instead'.
~/.claude/commands/code-simplify.md: 'Use the `code-simplifier:code-simplifier` plugin agent, not the local `code-simplification` skill'.

claims.claim: code-review:reviewer is the plugin's internal sub-agent that reviews one cell, not the routing target
claims.evidence: The reviewer agent's own description: 'Reviews one cell of a code review... Dispatched by the code-review skill'. Correctly identified as a trap rather than a candidate.

claims.claim: /review is a thin entry point to code-review-and-quality's five-axis workflow
claims.evidence: ~/.claude/commands/review.md body: 'Invoke the code-review-and-quality skill' followed by five numbered axes.

claims.claim: The local code-simplification skill is a reference document that only advises
claims.evidence: ~/.claude/skills/code-simplification/SKILL.md is prose guidance with no allowed-tools grant and no execution loop; ~/.claude/commands/code-simplify.md independently states 'the local skill only advises'.

suggestions.expectation: Names both the local code-review and the plugin code-review:code-review in qualified form, and picks one with a stated reason
suggestions.reason: A stated reason is required but its truth is not, so a run that names both candidates and then rejects one on an invented property would still pass this expectation. Only expectation 2 catches that, and it does so as a separate line item — meaning a run can score 3/4 while its central routing decision rests on a fabrication. Consider folding accuracy into this expectation, or weighting expectation 2 as a gate on the others.

suggestions.expectation: Rejects no candidate on a property it does not declare, and claims no capability of the chosen skill that it does not declare
suggestions.reason: This expectation carries the whole eval but is phrased as an absence, which is expensive and unbounded to verify — a grader must read three SKILL.md files plus an agent definition and check every sentence. The named false claims in the grader brief ('heavyweight repo-wide sweeps', 'needs the /code-review command') are what make it tractable. Consider promoting the discriminator itself to a positive expectation, e.g. 'states a discriminator that both skills actually declare — the local skill's Spec axis / originating-issue requirement, or its two fixed axes — and does not use scope shape as the tiebreaker, since both accept a branch.' That is checkable in one read and directly targets the failure mode observed in the baseline run.

No expectation covers whether the run correctly handles the second-order trap that the plugin's own sub-agents (code-review:reviewer, code-review:seam-reviewer, code-review:confidence-scorer) are namespace neighbours that a qualified-name search will surface. Run A explicitly identifies and rejects code-review:reviewer as a routing target; that is a real discrimination worth crediting and no expectation asks for it.

No expectation checks the ordering or the sequencing rationale, yet both runs volunteer it and it is substantively load-bearing — the code-simplifier plugin declares it must not run on broken code, which makes review-then-cleanup a declared constraint rather than mere deference to the user's phrasing. An expectation like 'grounds the review-before-cleanup ordering in the simplifier's declared do-not-use-on-broken-code constraint rather than only in the user's wording' would be discriminating.

eval_feedback.overall: Expectation 2 is the discriminating one and it worked: it is the only expectation that separated this run from the baseline, which passed 1, 3 and 4 while failing 2. The set would be stronger if the accuracy requirement were a gate rather than a peer line item, since a run can currently score 75% while its primary routing decision is built on a false property.
